newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes rise with NYMEX, trade flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes rise with NYMEX, trade flat.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices rose midday with NYMEX and cash markets but trade stayed lackluster as players were slow to return to the market following an industry conference.
Also, buyers said they avoided taking crude because West Coast products lagged the NYMEX and kept refinery margins low.
The discount for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained $2.30 a barrel less November West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
The American Petroleum Institute (API) reported crude inventories for PADD 5 West Coast rose 354,000 barrels to 30.2 million.
Meanwhile, a deal got done Monday for high-viscosity high-sulphur (HVHS) blend crude, a type of Outer Continental Shelf (OSC) blend which moves down California's Line 63 pipeline.
The deal was struck at postings plus $4.60 a barrel.
Straight Line 63 diffs remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under spot WTI for November delivery.
Kern River, from California's San Joaquin Valley, rose with postings to 16.80/17.00 a barrel.
And prices for Long Beach-based Wilmington crude also tracked higher postings to $18.15/18.25 a barrel.
